summary:
Masovian Voivodeship stands under Poland's national framework, which the national record carries. The region's own record in these sources consists of a municipal declaration of equality signed in the capital and a ruling by the province's administrative court that closed out the last local document of its kind in the country.

On 6 February 2024 the Voivodeship Administrative Court in Warsaw revoked the final document in Poland declaring a locality 'against LGBT ideology'. The ruling ended the sequence of local anti-LGBT resolutions. The sources do not name the municipality whose document was struck down, so these sources do not establish whether that last document sat inside Masovian Voivodeship or elsewhere; what is clear is that the administrative court sitting in Warsaw issued the decision.

In March 2019 the Mayor of Warsaw signed a declaration of equality and non-discrimination that includes commitments on responding to hate crime. The declaration stands and the sources record no repeal. It is an instrument of the capital's municipal authorities, not a province-wide provision, and it does not extend to the rest of the voivodeship.
tangentialFactors:
Both region-level instruments point the same way. The capital's March 2019 declaration commits the city authorities to non-discrimination and a hate-crime response and has not been withdrawn, and the administrative court's February 2024 ruling removed the last local declaration restricting LGBT residents. Neither source describes complaints, prosecutions or other enforcement activity attached to either instrument.

The province has no separate province-wide equality instrument recorded in these sources. Outside the capital, a trans visitor's protection rests on the national framework rather than on any Masovian measure documented here.
localsOnly:
For people living in Warsaw, the March 2019 declaration commits the city to equality, non-discrimination and a response to hate crime. It remains a standing municipal commitment with no repeal recorded in these sources.

The 6 February 2024 ruling of the Voivodeship Administrative Court removed the last local document in the country declaring a locality 'against LGBT ideology', so after that date no resident remained subject to one. The sources do not identify the municipality whose document was revoked, and therefore do not show whether residents of this province were among the last affected.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources do not identify the municipality whose 'against LGBT ideology' document was revoked on 6 February 2024, nor whether it lay within Masovian Voivodeship. Whether Masovian Voivodeship was among the voivodeships that adopted resolutions of that kind after 2015 is likewise not stated in this inventory.

The legal character of the capital's March 2019 declaration is not specified: whether it binds city institutions or is a statement of commitments, what reporting or complaint mechanism accompanies it, and what budget or staff it carries are all unrecorded. No Masovian-specific provisions on identity documents, health care, screening, facilities or hate-crime prosecutions appear in this inventory; that national legal and enforcement record is carried by the national entry.
